candidates.exact_problem: A static-view VLA cannot reliably disambiguate a task-critical target or affordance when the current view is occluded or visually aliased; the thesis would permit a bounded camera-view action before manipulation.
candidates.why_it_matters: A policy can be mechanically competent yet act on the wrong object or affordance because the fixed view does not contain enough task-relevant evidence.
candidates.closest_primary_prior: ActiveVLA: Injecting Active Perception into Vision-Language-Action Models for Precise 3D Robotic Manipulation
candidates.related_primary_prior: Observe Then Act: Asynchronous Active Vision-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation
candidates.official_code_availability: The ActiveVLA official artifact explicitly lists training, inference, evaluation, and real-robot code as pending. No released implementation is present.
candidates.official_checkpoint_availability: The ActiveVLA official artifact explicitly lists pretrained models as pending and exposes no deployable model through an inference provider.
candidates.benchmark_protocol: ActiveVLA reports RLBench, COLOSSEUM, and GemBench with multi-view 3D critical-region localization, active viewpoint selection, and 3D zoom. Observe Then Act reports eight viewpoint-constrained RLBench tasks with a camera NBV policy followed by a gripper NBP policy.
candidates.expected_base: A static-view policy with nonzero task competence but repeated target or affordance errors under matched occlusion or visual aliasing.
candidates.expected_prior: ActiveVLA or Observe Then Act actively changes viewpoint before producing manipulation actions.
candidates.residual_hypothesis: A low-cost, discrete camera micro-probe could retain disambiguation gains while using fewer 3D projections, views, and active-perception compute than ActiveVLA.
candidates.diagnostic_headroom: No local headroom is yet measurable because the existing LIBERO policy and action interface do not control a camera, while the official ActiveVLA implementation and checkpoints remain unreleased.
legal_deployment_inputs: live RGB or benchmark-authorized RGB-D/point-cloud observations
candidates.local_compute_path: Would require installing and validating an active-camera RLBench-class benchmark, obtaining or reproducing a compatible Base, defining camera actions without privileged simulator state, and training a 3D/view-selection prior. That path is not available on the current pinned local stack within twelve active hours.
candidates.method_novelty_opportunity: Probe-cost-aware active disambiguation could be distinct only if it improves a verified ActiveVLA residual rather than reimplementing next-best-view selection or 3D zoom.
candidates.strongest_reviewer_objection: ActiveVLA already localizes critical 3D regions and selects viewpoints, and Observe Then Act already serializes camera next-best-view and gripper action policies; a camera micro-probe is likely an incremental simplification without an executable residual.
candidates.stage0_falsification_test: On frozen ambiguous/occluded simulator identities, compare no-probe, random-probe, heuristic-probe, and learned active-probe target/action consistency. Reject if random or heuristic probing explains the gain or if the official prior saturates the condition.
candidates.stage_a_path: Paired official active-camera simulator episodes for static Base, closest active-perception Prior, Ours, key ablation, and random/heuristic controls. This path is currently unavailable locally.
candidates.pareto_opportunity: Noninferior closed-loop success with materially fewer views, lower latency, or no 3D projection stack than the Prior.
candidates.second_condition_or_backbone: Held-out COLOSSEUM occlusion/generalization condition or GemBench after a positive RLBench result.
candidates.camera_only_relevance: Non-actuated handheld or prerecorded viewpoint changes could measure target-selection consistency, but cannot establish active-camera manipulation success.
candidates.archived_route_overlap: The 2026-07-07 tournament recommended active micro-probes but never executed them. The thesis is materially different from wrist dropout and asynchronous action delay, but current ActiveVLA/Observe Then Act literature creates direct mechanism overlap; AMP-GD also archived active action planning that failed to beat simple controls locally.

candidates.exact_problem: A VLA that misses a grasp, drops or misplaces an object, or enters a state-breaking contact failure lacks a verified autonomous retry or reset path and continues an invalid nominal trajectory.
candidates.why_it_matters: Ordinary success-only imitation data underrepresent the off-trajectory states that dominate long-horizon manipulation failures.
candidates.closest_primary_prior: FLARE: A Failure-Aware Framework for Autonomous Correction and Recovery in Visual-Language Robotic Manipulation
candidates.related_retry_prior: Beyond Monotonic Progress: Retry-Supervised Value Learning for Robot Imitation (ReTVL)
candidates.related_executable_detector: SAFE: Multitask Failure Detection for Vision-Language-Action Models
candidates.official_code_availability: The official CVPR FLARE page exposes paper and supplement but no code repository. No official ReTVL repository was located through its primary record. SAFE has official training/evaluation code, but it is a detector rather than an autonomous recovery prior.
candidates.official_checkpoint_availability: No FLARE or ReTVL checkpoint was located. The SAFE repository has no GitHub release and documents training from generated rollouts rather than a released detector checkpoint.
candidates.benchmark_protocol: FLARE evaluates contact-rich manipulation using Retry demonstrations, an object-centric Reset skill library, and an online MLLM monitor. ReTVL uses retry keypoints in mixed-quality real-robot demonstrations to reweight behavior cloning. SAFE evaluates failure detection on LIBERO and SimplerEnv but does not execute recovery actions.
candidates.expected_base: A locally runnable VLA with nonzero nominal competence and repeated failures after induced reversible execution disturbances.
candidates.expected_prior: FLARE's trained Retry policy plus MLLM-arbitrated object-centric Reset skills, or ReTVL-reweighted behavior cloning for retry-rich data.
candidates.residual_hypothesis: A lightweight simulator-only recovery controller might use policy features and bounded retry supervision without an online MLLM or a separate reset-skill library.
candidates.diagnostic_headroom: Failed and successful rollout labels can support offline detection, but no current artifact establishes that a local detector can control a recovery action or that recoverable matched states can be evaluated under the frozen RAM ceiling.
candidates.local_compute_path: SAFE detector training could be adapted to cached rollouts, but faithful FLARE or ReTVL comparison requires unavailable retry/reset data, recovery policy code, and checkpoints. Generating the required closed-loop simulator trajectories is also blocked by the same verified host/WSL RAM boundary that closed A2C2.
candidates.method_novelty_opportunity: Only a verified recovery mechanism beyond detection, stopping, action filtering, nearest-trajectory retrieval, and retry-data reweighting could qualify.
candidates.strongest_reviewer_objection: The thesis is an obvious SAFE-detector plus FLARE/Retry-data composition, while the local campaign has already archived safety shields, phase retiming, chunk repair, safety/action correction, verifiers, and retrieval/memory recovery families.
candidates.stage0_falsification_test: On preregistered reversible disturbances, require detector timeliness plus a recovery-action advantage over stop-only, restart, random retry, and nearest/mean recovery controls. Reject if detection does not causally improve closed-loop recovery.
candidates.stage_a_path: Matched official simulator Base, SAFE-stop control, faithful FLARE/ReTVL Prior, Ours, ablation, and simple-retry episodes. No faithful local Prior path currently exists.
candidates.pareto_opportunity: Comparable recovery success without an online MLLM, reset-skill library, or second inference-time policy.
candidates.second_condition_or_backbone: Held-out failure type or task family, followed by a compatible second VLA only after positive simulator evidence.
candidates.camera_only_relevance: Camera-only video can validate failure-alert timeliness but cannot validate autonomous recovery or manipulation success.
candidates.archived_route_overlap: High overlap with CSS-Shield, Phase Retiming, TL-ChunkRepair, SACF, RAC, EAC, verifier/ranking routes, and retrieval/memory recovery routes. It is different from wrist dropout and asynchronous delay but re-enters multiple closed mechanism families.

selection_adjudication.reason: Neither thesis has both an executable closest prior and a locally feasible official-simulator Base/Ours path within the fixed twelve-hour decision budget. Selecting either would replace official-prior-first residual verification with a speculative local port or would reuse closed recovery mechanisms.

next_authorized_action: Stop autonomous local method development at NO_DEFENSIBLE_LOCAL_RESEARCH_PATH_FOUND. Preserve the record and wait for materially new resources, an executable official prior, or explicit user redirection; do not create Pivot Epoch 3.
